name: WILD WORKOUTS
description: Ready to flex your muscles at the wildest workout spot in town? The Louisville Zoo and Flex Appeal invite you to join us for one of our exciting fitness classes at the Zoo. All fitness levels are welcome to take part in this unique event. Each workout will be approximately one hour in length and will take place in different areas of the Zoo. Sign up now to experience one of our wild classes! Because of the unique atmosphere and the terrain around the Zoo, closed toed shoes are strongly encouraged. Be sure to bring a water bottle-with dates in June, July, August and September, we'll have you sweating before the workouts even start! The Zoo has several bottle refill stations around the park so you should have a fill spot nearby!

name: Endurance United Summer programs
description: Endurance United programs are for any skier, beginner to advanced, youth to adult. Endurance United programs help any motivated skier get the most out of training with sessions designed around their needs. Participants benefit from the deep instructional and racing experience of the coaches, and connect with other athletes of similar interests. New for the 2026 season! description: Bring on summer running! ☀️👟 Heat? Humidity? No problem! We’re turning up the fun with the Summer Sizzler! description: In-Person Race Start times: 6:50 PM Kids Race, 7:00 PM 3K/5K/10K The 2FGR Run for Inclusion was started in 2009 by the running group 2FGR (Two Fat Guys Running), with the very modest goal to raise $5,000 in support of the Down syndrome community. Now going on its 17th year, the 2FGR Run for Inclusion has donated nearly $600,000 in its first 16 years. This event proudly benefits Team Heart & Sole, 4 Paws for Ability, and DSACO. name: The Force Run – 2026
street_address: Private Invitation to friends and family
description: The Force Run is a virtual 5K held in loving memory of Kyree Samuel Abraham, a joyful, courageous child who bravely battled cancer. His light, laughter, and faith continue to inspire everyone who knew him. This event honors his legacy by supporting the place that cared for him with extraordinary compassion — the Medical College of Georgia. All proceeds from this race will be donated directly to MCG to support pediatric care, research, and the families who walk similar journeys. We run to remember. We run to celebrate. We run to shine Kyree’s light.

name: The M&T Bank Vermont City Marathon & Relay
name_en: The M&T Bank Vermont City Marathon & Relay
organizer: The M&T Bank Vermont City Marathon & Relay
description: Welcome to the M&T Bank Vermont City Marathon Weekend, featuring the M&T Bank Vermont City Marathon & Relay, with 2 Person and 3-5 Person Relay presented by Darn Tough, Vermont, and the M&T Bank Memorial Day Weekend Youth Events! The marathon and relay course is a fast course--mostly flat with some rolling hills and one bigger climb at the midway point of each loop--through Burlington and along Lake Champlain. The M&T Bank Vermont City Marathon & Relay is a community effort, recognizing all those who have had a hand in making the race a success since 1989. The course runs through the best of Burlington, from the Church Street Marketplace to the Burlington Bike Path and offers exceptional views of the Adirondack Mountains. All up-to-date race information can be found on the RunVermont website at www.runvermont.org/vermont-city-marathon-relay/ and www.runvermont.org/memorial-day-weekend-youth-events/.

name: The Hunger Run
description: Please join us on Saturday, May 23, 2026, at our NEW location of Wolfe Park to participate in The Hunger Run 5K and help chase hunger out of Central Ohio! We've also added a 1-mile event option for those who want to participate in the Hunger Run but aren't ready for a 5K! We are hosting the 7th Annual Hunger Run 5K in support of Neighborhood Services Inc. (NSI), a local food pantry and resource center located right here in Columbus, Ohio. Our goal is to spread awareness about hunger and food insecurity in central Ohio, bring the community together, and raise money for Neighborhood Services Inc. Did you know that 13.5% of Franklin County residents are food insecure, nearly 1 in 5 Ohio children live in food-insecure households, and Ohio ranks #1 in food insecurity in the Midwest? These are just a few of the many reasons why Neighborhood Services Inc. is so important. name: MS 3000
description: A 30 day motorcycle challenge to benefit people living with Multiple Sclerosis The Ride & Raise Challenge is a motorcycle challenge you can enter and ride from anywhere. The Ride & Raise Challenge gives you a reason to ride your motorcycle/bicycle or walk/run as much as you can in 30 days for a great cause. The challenge can be completed at your discretion and the rules are simple. Registered riders or walkers/runners will document riding as many miles as they can from May 24th - June 22nd while collecting support from family and friends. Each registered rider will get a Ride & Raise Challenge silicone wrist band we hope you will wear to let your friends and family know what it is you are attempting and why. Get involved, learn about MS and realize how tough every single day might be for someone with Multiple Sclerosis. Do your part to help find a cure. name: Thunder Road Gravel Tour
description: Join us for a series of rides from May through August and explore what the central Illinois has to offer when you venture off of the beaten path. Ride specifics are TBD, but expect something in the ballpark of 30 and 60 mile options with a convenience store stop in the middle. After each ride, we'll have an optional takeover of a local brewery/bar/restaurant. This is a no-cost series, so there will be no SAG offered. As a gravel rider, you're probably already self-sufficient enough to fix a flat or minor mechanical on the road and if you're not, make some friends out there! But that's just the basic highlights. Points-Based CompetitionThe most exciting part of the series will be a points-based competition. Each route will have a few gravel segments selected where riders will have the option of competing to do their best efforts. description: Celebrate the United States’ 250th Independence Day by running a mile for every year!! Freedom's Foundation is the Blood of the Brave, and its strength is the Spirit of the Free! name: Wednesdays at Wakefield
description: Four Wednesday Races make for One Great Series Plan to get off of work a bit early and join over 200 riders for four spectacular weekdays of racing starting May 27th! Pitched as a race “in your own backyard”, W@W features a very down-home and earthy venue. We are keeping the series as grassroots as you can get. But don’t let that fool you, this race series is a highly organized event, that allows for enough riding categories to give everyone a fighting chance. Bike Lane Race Team works hard to host a community-oriented race series. We have an all-volunteer staff who works closely with our local IMBA club, Mid Atlantic Off Road Enthusiasts (MORE), to make sure we have fun singletrack to race, that is great for everyone from juniors to beginners to elite racers. We also partner with NOVA Cycling, who run the youth races early in the evening. Wednesdays at Wakefield is not just a few races, it is an epic race series! name: TCTC Summer Track Series
description: The Summer Track Series meets at the Bob Sosnik Track @ Hanes Park in Winston-Salem. All of the meets start at 6:00 PM. There is no entry fee. You may run as many events as you like. This is a great tune-up for the TCTC Ultimate Runner event -- which is held on the fourth Saturday in June (and is limited to about 100 entrants). These events are for runners of all abilities and ages. If you don't want to run, come out and socialize with the other spectators and help with finish line timing and race officiating. name: Hypopara Life Awareness Walk
description: I am excited to share the very first virtual walk for World Hypoparathyroidism Awareness Day! The goal is simple: bring our community together, wherever we are in the world. Whether you walk around your neighborhood, on a treadmill, around your house, or even just to the mailbox and back, this is about participating in whatever way works for you. Every step counts! I am working on a few simple ways for people to participate remotely, including an app and a place to share a photo from your walk. This will be very informal, flexible, and accessible because we know everyone's health, symptoms, and abilities are different. No matter how far you walk, we hope you will join us as we take steps together for awareness, support, and community. #WHAD #WorldHypoparaythyroidismAwarenessDay #Hypoparathyroidism #OneStepAtATime #TogetherForHP #HypoparaLife

description: One of our original races is back and moving to the wilds of West Virginia! Teams of 2-4 people will trek, packraft, mountain bike and navigate their way through a course that explores this amazing and unique corner of the state. With the highest concentration of public land in the state—dominated by the mighty and vast Monongahela National Forest, 400 miles of trails, extensive backcountry and wilderness, legendary mountain biking, and free-flowing rivers—teams can expect a course that is rugged, and relatively remote for a race of this length. And the scenery? Some of the best on the eastern seaboard. Pocahontas County is known as nature’s playground for a reason. description: Von Hippel-Lindau disease (VHL) is a rare genetic disorder that significantly increases the chance that you’ll have certain kinds of cancerous (malignant) tumors and noncancerous (benign) tumors and cysts. The cause of VHL is a mutation to the VHL gene. Everyone has a VHL gene and its job is to put the brakes on tumor growth in the human body. If you have VHL, your VHL gene lacks that component and at times will excel tumor growth throughout the body. Historically, the average life expectancy for an individual with VHL was around 40 to 52 years, but advancements in early diagnosis and treatment in the last 20 years have increased it to 67 years for males and 60 years for females. We want to be part of raising that number. We are grateful for what God-through technology & science, has done; but our race doesn't stop there! name: Miles for Miles
description: The reason for this race: Miles Jacobsen is 10 years old and currently in 4th grade. His family moved to KC in 2021 when his dad was hired as the Lead Teaching Pastor at Heartland Community Church off Strang Line Rd in Olathe. Miles Jacobsen is one of the many kids in Kansas City battling a brain tumor. Days after his 9th birthday in March 2024, he was diagnosed with an inoperable brain tumor. After a long year of chemotherapy, Miles is now awaiting the development of more targeted therapy that will help him fight the growth of this tumor. Despite these challenges, Miles is a joyful and active kid whose positive outlook has inspired hundreds, if not thousands, of people since his diagnosis. His heart beats strong for people of all ages who are enduring their own cancer journeys, and he’s always looking to lift other people’s spirits. He has taken to running over the last year as a way to raise funds and awareness for children’s brain tumors. As the namesake for the Miles for Miles Foundation, he is a young sp…

name: Climb the Mine 2026
description: Welcome to the First Annual Climb the Mine Hike in Hibbing, Minnesota. This one-of-a-kind community hike begins at the Greyhound Bus Museum & through Historic Old Hibbing, where the roots of our mining town first took hold more than a century ago. From there, participants will make their way through the heart of Hibbing and gradually climb to the breathtaking overlook at the Hull-Rust-Mahoning Mine View. At the finish, you will stand at what is often called the world’s largest open-pit iron ore mine, known as the “Grand Canyon of the North.” The climb is steady and rewarding, ending with one of the most incredible views on the Iron Range. This event is designed for all ages and abilities. Whether you are hiking with friends, family, or coworkers, the Climb the Mine Hike is about enjoying the journey, celebrating Hibbing’s history, and taking in the view together. The Climb the Mine Hike is a fundraiser for the Hibbing Tourist & Senior Citizen Center, supporting local programming, events, and services …

Join us for a unique race experience where you can choose your adventure to run, swim, walk, or paddle your way through the scenic beauty of Mendocino County's Big River. For the past 26 years, Cancer Resource Centers of Mendocino County has been bringing our community together for this special fundraising event. While the activities may change from year to year, our mission remains steadfast: to honor and remember those impacted by cancer, and to raise vital funds to support free services for individuals facing cancer in Mendocino County. Starting at the Big River boat launch, participants will embark on a journey filled with stunning views and the shared goal of making a difference in the lives of others. Don't miss out on this unforgettable adventure! Register now and be part of something truly meaningful. name: Race for Education
description: Lace up your sneakers and join the City of Paramount for our annual 5K/1K Run/Walk & Health and Wellness Fair! Whether you’re racing to the finish line or strolling with family and friends, this event is all about moving your body, feeling good, and celebrating a healthier Paramount together. Stick around after the run to explore wellness resources, fitness activities, giveaways, and fun for all ages. Best of all, every dollar raised directly supports the Paramount Education Partnership (PEP) Scholarship—so every step you take helps invest in our students’ future! 🏃‍♀️💙🎓

name: Bike N' Trike 2026
description: Get ready to roll into one of the most joyful days of the year in downtown Modesto! The MoChiMu Bike n’ Trike Family Ride & Fun Festival takes off promptly on Saturday, May 30, 2026 at 8:30 AM and invites families, friends, and little riders of all ages to gather at the Modesto Children’s Museum before rolling out together in a colorful parade of bikes, trikes, scooters, wagons, and other rolling rides - many sporting delightful balloon backpacks and playful group costumes. From MoChiMu we cruise a 2.2 mile route through downtown and along the Virginia Corridor before arriving at Roosevelt Park for a festival packed with fun. More than 25 community vendors host hands-on activities for kids alongside fire trucks, bottle rockets, games, dancing, and delicious food. Grab your crew, decorate your ride, and sign up today to celebrate joyful play while supporting the Modesto Children’s Museum’s mission to inspire creativity, critical thinking, and lifelong learning. 🚲☀️

name: Dos Rios Sundown Run
description: Folks, it's that time again! Ever fantasized about having a state park as your personal playground after hours? Well, dream no more! Your amazing friends at Dusty Bottoms are making it happen on May 30th at Dos Rios State Park, just outside of Modesto. When the regular park visitors pack up and go home, that's when the fun begins! Choose your trail adventure: a spicy 3-mile sprint or a robust 5-mile ramble. Both distances are run on buffed out fire roads and will take you by the lovely Tuolumne River. After conquering the trails, we'll do what Dusty Bottoms does best - hang out, swap stories, and celebrate like the trail champions we are. It's a classic "fat ass" event where every donation helps our park ranger friends keep this slice of wilderness awesome for years to come. So grab your running shoes, fill those coolers and let's turn this park into our personal after-hours playground!

name: A Time of Hope
description: We invite you to join us for this special event dedicated to raising cancer awareness and supporting our friends affected by cancer. A Time of Hope brings the community together for an informative and inspiring experience. During our 1 mile-"ish" social walk, current patients can connect with survivors to share experiences. After the walk, medical professionals share valuable information at our Tent Talks. Free skin cancer are available by appointment and walk-in at the event thanks to Snow Dermatology, Project Happy Face and Lilly. Mail-in colon cancer screening kits are available to eligible participants at the OHSU Knight Cancer Institute mobile medical vans. Browse the activity stations to learn of various cancer resources available and about preventative measures you can take. And then just have fun at our activity stations including a hat decorating booth, Kindness Shop and silent auction! name: 2026 Smith Rock Classic
description: Welcome to the Smith Rock Classic! Join us for our springtime 50 mile, 50K, and 10 mile races that showcase the beauty of Smith Rock State Park. The towering basalt cliffs and views of the nearby Cascade range await you as you travel in and around the park. The courses also include miles in the Crooked River Grasslands - beyond the boundary of the park - that offer a different view of Oregon's classic high desert terrain as well as the fantastic scenery of the high peaks of the Cascades.

name: Lotus Run
description: 2026 Lotus Run for Mental Health Our Community has been greatly affected by suicide. The pains stretch deep and wide within our neighborhoods, schools and businesses. Too many people with mental health challenges feel like this world would be better without them in it— that they are a burden on the world and their loved ones… and that is simply not true! Through physical wellness, community support, fellowship and with your support, we KNOW we can make a meaningful change in our community, one stride at a time! So join us in beautiful Lake Stevens, WA on May 30th for a HUGE DAY IN MENTAL HEALTH AWARENESS with a fun and inspiring 10K run, 5k walk/run, or 1 Mile walk/run. Visit our website for more information and details.

This race offers you four different options; a distance for everyone in the family, group of friends or coworkers. The course will be flat & fast! All race distances are on a paved path and along the riverfront. Chiawana is a Native word for “Big River” The Columbia River has provided this region's culture and economy for thousands of years. It is the largest river in the Pacific Northwest. The river forms in the Rocky Mountains of British Columbia, Canada and flows through Washington. description: OSCAR MIKE! Join our next mission as we ruck Wachusett Mountain on Sunday, May 31, 2026 at 9am. name: FXBG Trail 5 Miler
description: The Motts 5 Miler is the second race of the FXBG Trail series. This trail race begins with a smooth, approachable start along Motts Run Reservoir — giving runners time to settle into their pace and find their rhythm before the course gradually reveals its character. The opening stretch is runnable and forgiving, setting you up for what’s to come. From there, the course features three main climbs that define the day. Each ascent brings its own personality — steady and sustained, short and punchy, and one final grinder that tests your grit. Altogether, runners will tackle 341 feet of total elevation gain, enough to make you work without overwhelming the legs. The descents are flowing and fun, offering opportunities to recover and carry momentum into the next section. This race strikes a perfect balance: approachable yet engaging, challenging but rewarding — a trail experience that keeps you honest while remaining accessible for a wide range of runners.

This May, we're throwing the biggest celebration yet — and we want the whole community to be part of it. Walk, jog, or run the 5K — every pace is welcome. name: West Virginia Cryptid Race Series
description: The West Virginia Cryptid Race Series is a West Virginia–based running series inspired by the state’s legendary cryptids and the unique locations they are said to roam. Each race has its own theme, atmosphere, and community feel, giving runners a fun reason to explore new places while enjoying professionally produced events. Participants can choose to run a single race or take on the full series. Those who complete multiple races will experience a mix of local folklore, scenic courses, and memorable race-day energy across the region. The race order begins in Clay with the Bigfoot-themed race, setting the tone in classic Appalachian surroundings. The second stop brings the series to Saint Albans for the Mothman race, offering a fast, fun, and community-focused experience centered around West Virginia’s most iconic legend. The third race takes place in Gassaway, inspired by the Braxton County Monster and one of the state’s most famous cryptid encounters. The series final will be held at Kanawha State Forest wit…

name: JJ's Journey for a Cause
description: Join us in celebrating our sweet angel's 5th birthday! We can't think of any better way to honor JJ than to participate in a 5K in his memory. Doesn't matter if you run or walk, just get outside and move your feet #forJJ! We invite you to stay and hang out after the race to celebrate JJ's birthday - we will have music, snacks, balloons, and entertainment! All proceeds will go to First Candle, an organization that works to help bereaved families and hoping to bring an end to SIDS. In November of 2021 we unexpectedly lost our 5 month old son, JJ. He was a perfectly healthy and happy baby, thriving and enjoying life. What started as a typical Friday morning for our family changed completely when we got the call that JJ had gone down for his morning nap at daycare and did not wake up.We did everything we were supposed to do and unfortunately have no answers to what caused this tragedy. name: Mere Mortals
description: In 1996, Ann Knight and her friend Janet Boylan put on the very first Santa Rosa Island Triathlon. On race day, as they watched a few hundred new triathletes struggle to complete the race, they decided that a training program for new triathletes might be a good idea. And so the Mere Mortals program was born in 1997. Ann teamed up with her husband Charlie to plan for the second annual SRI Tri, and Janet took on the task of organizing a free training group for those who might want help getting ready for their first Triathlon. In those first few years, 20-30 people would meet on Pensacola Beach and work their way up from short drills of swimming, biking, and running, eventually building up to a combined practice Tri that covered the full distance of the SRI Tri on the very same course they’d use on race day. In the years since then, Mere Mortals has grown from an informal gathering to an organized event with attendance often exceeding 200 members. It is now managed by Tri Gulf Coast, the local triathlon club, an…

name: Billings Skyline Races
description: Half marathon & 30K Great Views. Challenging Course. Unforgettable Experience.The Skyline Races Half Marathon and 30K brings runners to the top of Billings’ legendary Rimrocks for a race like no other. Experience Montana’s wide-open beauty on a paved path of moderate elevation changes that makes it ideal for both competitive athletes and first-time half-marathoners or 30K participants. Featuring breathtaking views of the Yellowstone Valley and the Beartooth Mountains, the Skyline Trail section travels along a sandstone ridge, offering sweeping panoramic views. Runners then connect to Skyway Drive, a newer path with gentle curves, rolling hills, open terrain, and distant mountain backdrops. Both distances loop into the Alkali Creek Trail, following a shaded stretch along the creek before heading back toward the finish line at Two Moon Park.

Starting and finishing at historic Olympian Hall, the day includes lively aid stations and rolls straight into a post-race celebration with food, drinks, and live music. All riders will receive an Outlaw Gravel Year 1 hat at packet pickup. Years from now, you’ll want to say you were there for Year One.

description: From June 1, 2026 through August 31, 2026 run VIRTUALLY from Holland, Michigan, along US-31, to Charlevoix, Michigan! That's 236 miles! description: York 38 Special The York Community is excited to announce this year’s York 38 Special is Saturday, August 15. The 38 Special is our volunteer fire department’s annual fundraiser. The 38 Special bike race features three race options, each traversing spectacular scenery through the Big Belt Mountains. The course includes incredible mountain overlooks, rugged canyons, and three creek crossings. The 38-mile race includes the Bear Trap and Trout Creek options. Both routes are on gravel and dirt single track roads, gaining at least 3,000 vertical feet. The Trout Creek option includes the beautiful Trout Creek Canyon single track route. name: 100 miles to Auburn
description: 100 Miles to Auburn – A Global Virtual Challenge Inspired by the Western States 100 Born in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic, the 100 Miles to Auburn virtual race was created as a way to stay connected, motivated, and inspired—no matter where in the world you’re running. Since then, it’s become an annual tradition, with over 3,000 runners from around the globe joining the journey each year. Held each June, this virtual race mirrors the iconic 100-mile trek from Olympic Valley to Auburn, the same route covered during the legendary Western States Endurance Run. While Western States runners take on the course in a single weekend at the end of June, 100 Miles to Auburn gives you the whole month to complete your miles—wherever and however you choose. Whether you're training for your own ultramarathon, supporting a runner at Western States, or just looking for a meaningful goal to chase in June, this race brings the spirit of the trail and the camaraderie of the ultra community to your own backyard. name: Loppet Paddling
description: Canoeing and paddling in general complements Loppet pillars of outdoor endurance competition and urban adventure in natural spaces. Competitive canoeing is a full-body exercise, though focally on the upper body, which makes a great balance for all those runners/hikers/bikers out there and great cross-training for cross country skiing. It is also a low-impact sport that people can enjoy well into their older ages. Competitive canoeing is highly technical and tactical, but also something people can make noticeable improvements in right away with some key changes to the traditional Boundary Waters stroke. Plus, the vantage point from the lakes is a beautiful, fulfilling place to spend your time this summer. Financial Assistance: The Loppet provides financial assistance for those in need. The Alliance is honored to announce that the 2026 9/11 National Memorial Trail Bike Tour is scheduled to take place from June 12 to July 11, 2026, in observance of the 25th anniversary of September 11, 2001. This historic journey offers a powerful opportunity to reflect on a quarter century of remembrance and American resilience. About Running Against ALS Running Against ALS was initially set up to benefit Officer Steve Asch. Steve was diagnosed with ALS on February 14, 2022. organizer: Tucson Tri Girls Easy Peasy Lemmon Squeezy 2026
description: Tucson Tri Girls and its sponsors and community supporters present Easy Peasy Lemmon Squeezy, a six week series in which cyclists progressively increase their mileage each Saturday, ascending Mount Lemmon. Riders have the option of the Whole Lemmon or the Half Lemmon. Riders who choose the Whole Lemmon work their way up to riding from Milepost 0 at the base of Mt. Lemmon all the way to the Cookie Cabin in Summerhaven. Riders who choose the Half Lemmon will work their way up to riding from Milepost 0 all the way to Windy Point (Geology Vista). Every year we have riders of all abilities, beginners through seasoned veterans. The first ride starts on June 20th and the last ride is on August 1st. (WE WILL SKIP JULY 4.) All participants meet at Milepost 0 at 6AM for check-in at the intersection of Catalina Highway and Mount Lemmon short road. Wheels are rolling at 6:10am. Ride at your individual pace. SAG stops with hydration and nutrition are provided by sponsors and community supporters starting on the …

name: Flagstaff Run Series
description: Welcome to the 22nd annual Flagstaff Running Series sponsored by locally-based Loven Contracting! The Series package is a great value and it is one-stop shopping for all five races. Through March 15th, the Series package for either the long or short is only $185. After then it rises to $215 (thru May 31st) and finally to $225 until registration closes on June 14th. For students 18 and under, the package price is $160 rising to $175 after March 15th, and increases to $185 after May 31st until registration closes on June 14th. The package of 5 kid's dashes is only $50 through the above registration periods. When you register for the Long Series Package, you are automatically entered into the three 10K races, a 1-miler, and the half marathon. If you register for the Short Course Series Package, you are automatically entered into the three 5K races, a 1-miler, and a 2-miler. Because the race packages are the same price, you can switch up or down in distance, you just need to reach out to the individual …

name: Junior Loppet - Summer
description: Junior Loppet is a year-round, after-school program designed to empower middle school students in Minneapolis through a variety of outdoor activities, such as cross-country skiing, mountain biking, trail running, orienteering, paddling, camping, and nature exploration. The program targets schools where the majority of students qualify for free and reduced lunch. Junior Loppet fosters key outcomes of experience, healing, belonging, and empowerment. The program meets 2-3 days per week during the school year and runs throughout the summer, offering a combination of training, events, races, and weekend camping trips. Through these outdoor adventures, students develop healthy habits, enhance their social and emotional skills, and build meaningful connections that set them on a path to success. Junior Loppet creates a supportive environment where youth can grow, thrive, and build resilience through physical activity, teamwork, and personal achievement. Junior Loppet Summer programming will meet on Tuesdays and Thu…

name: Junior Loppet - Littles
description: Junior Loppet Littles is an exciting extension of the Junior Loppet program, designed to offer the same empowering outdoor experiences to younger children starting at age 5. By introducing youth to outdoor activities at an earlier age, we believe we can have an even greater impact on their development. This program provides young participants with the opportunity to build healthy habits, develop social skills, and foster a love for outdoor adventure—all while having fun and learning new skills. Junior Loppet Littles is a foundational step in nurturing resilience, confidence, and a lifelong connection to the outdoors. Junior Loppet Littles Summer programming will meet on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Participants can look forward to paddling, hiking, orienteering, nature connection, team building, archery, gardening, outdoor play, biking, and mountain biking.

name: JUNIOR CAMPS
description: Endurance United junior camps are great opportunities not only to train, but to travel to different places, create EU team memories, and for a short time, live the life of a professional skier. Camps are included with D-team registration. Summer Junior participants have reduced rate for the June Camp. Use coupon code "summer" for $100 discount or use coupon code "paybycheck" and we'll email you an invoice with the discounted amount.Camp fees include transportation, food, coaching, trail passes (if applicable), and lodging (if applicable). Local Tour is open to 13yr olds with prior approval. Contact John Richter or Emma Stertz.

name: TVFR Woodland Trail Series
description: The TVFR Woodland Trail Series will be in its 28th year. The event takes place at West Hill Dam in Uxbridge MA in the early evenings on the last Thursday of June, July and August. This is a trail race on well-marked courses through single/double track trails and gravel roads. Each race will offer a different course to experience all West Hill has to offer. The Trail Series is designed for runners. If you plan to walk any part of the course, we ask that you notify us and plan on starting earlier than the posted start times. This is to help keep our volunteers from being out on the course for longer than required. Run all 3 races and be eligible for the overall male and female championship. There will be no Day-Of Registration. Each race will be limited to 125 runners. Parking is limited, please arrive early to get to the designated parking area. The gate access to the start area will close approximately at 5:30. Limited parking is available at the Dam entrance but it's a 3/4 mile warmup run to th…

name: After Work Dirt Trail Races fka Tiny Trails
name_en: After Work Dirt Trail Races fka Tiny Trails
organizer: After Work Dirt Trail Races fka Tiny Trails
description: After Work Dirt is a small, community-focused trail race series designed to get people off the pavement and onto the incredible trail networks right here in our backyard. Born out of the evolution of the Tiny Trails Series, these laid-back weeknight races are an opportunity to explore local terrain, meet good people, and enjoy a little friendly competition. Each event partners with local land trusts — the organizations that care for and protect these spaces — helping connect runners not just to the trails themselves, but to the communities behind them. Races are intentionally small, capped at 75 runners, creating a welcoming and low-key atmosphere. Courses range from approximately 5K to 6.5 miles, with every venue located within 20 minutes of Portland. Come straight from work, run hard (or don’t), and stick around afterward for a casual hang. Runners who complete at least three races will be included in the overall series standings and eligible for sponsor prizes. Awards will be presented to the top men, wome…

name: Summer Sizzle Series
description: We’re kicking off a brand-new summer tradition for St. Louis runners. Whether you’re getting fit for fall, looking for a fun midweek run, or just want an excuse to get outside with your people, the Summer Sizzle Series is your Thursday night plan all summer long. June 25: 2 Mile @ Shaw Park July 9: 4K @ Tower Grove Park July 23: 4 Mile @ 370 Lakeside Park August 6: 5K @ George Winter Park Four races, four parks, different distances each time. Enjoy summer nights, great parks, music, movement, and a laid-back post-run hang with your crew. Here’s what’s in store: 4 unique races at different parks across the area Flexible options - jump in for one or commit to the full series Plus - each night includes a 1 Mile Fun Run, so bring the whole crew Register for the full Summer Sizzle Series: Complete 3 out of 4 races to earn a series finisher medal Score an exclusive series shirt Stay motivated all summer long Turn up the Heat. name: Bogus Trail Series
description: The Bogus Trail Series is back and better than ever this summer! Held on the beautiful trails of Bogus Basin, this three week series is a challenging and exhilarating way to hit some trails with other members of the community. The series will kick off on Friday, June 26th with subsequent races on Friday, July 10th & Friday, July 24th. Come to one or all three and receive a customized hat sponsored by Fleet Feet Treasure Valley! Races will meander through the breathtaking single track of Bogus with a spectrum of vertical-based efforts, ranging in distances from 4-6 miles (course maps are on our website HERE). Join us for these stunning views and a post-race celebration you will not forget! Each race will begin on Friday evenings near the entrance to Simplot Lodge. Post-race, enjoy a beautiful sunset as you venture back to Boise. The Bogus Trail Series is brought to you by Boise Running & the Boise Front Trail Festival team, known for the largest trail race in the state of Idaho! Questions? Check ou…

name: MRC Track & Field Series presented by Marathon Sports
name_en: MRC Track & Field Series presented by Marathon Sports
organizer: MRC Track & Field Series presented by Marathon Sports
description: Please do not select all meets unless you know you will attend all of them. On some evenings, we have had as many as 300 no-shows (participants who registered and did not attend); no-shows take slots away from participants who are ready and willing to participate. Youth runners are free!! So that we can continue to provide free track & field meets to all, we ask that, if able, you make a $5 donation. For all the information about the meets including events, times, etc. please visit www.mrctrack.com For registration/pricing purposes youth are all those under the age of 18. For participation purposes and results, anyone under the age of 14 (or high school) is considered youth. High school athletes should plan to compete in the adult division at each meet. Registration for the series is open at the end of April! Please visit our website for all the details. www.mrctf.org Please note, there are no non-binary heats or separate events, participate wherever you feel comfortable.

name: Westport Road Runners Summer Series
description: A series of ten progressively longer races, held at various locations throughout the Town of Westport. We're happy to announce the 64th annual Roadrunners Summer Series! Once again, we will be using the follow protocols: There will be no in-person race day registration on paper forms. Online registration will remain open until the start time. Runners should register before arriving at the race site, or on their phones when they get there (scan the QR code on the sandwich board sign), then check in with other pre-registered runners. Once again, we will utilize ChronoTrack chip timing technology for all races. This will give all runners a net or "chip" time based on when they cross the start, and will have the added benefit of almost instant results. If you sign up for text alerts, your finish time and place will be waiting for you on your phone when you get back to your car. You will also receive an email later on race morning with your individual result, often with a video clip of your finish. T…

name: The Racefaster Half Marathon
description: Flat and Fast Half Marathon in Bergen County NJ. The Racefaster Half Marathon is Bergen County’s premier long-distance race—built for speed. Whether you’re running your first half or chasing a personal best, our flat and fast course sets you up for success. Experience a scenic route, high-energy atmosphere, finisher medals, and live tracking so your supporters can follow you in real time.

name: The Sunlight Showdown
description: Welcome to the Sunlight Mountain Race Series, where mountain air, winding trails, and a vibrant community come together for an unforgettable summer of running. For seven years, our half marathon has challenged and inspired runners on the stunning trails of Sunlight Mountain. Now, we’re taking it to the next level. Introducing a full race series: a 5K, 10K, and Half Marathon designed to help you build, progress, and push your limits all season long. Starting with the 5K, stepping up to the 10K, and culminating in our signature Half Marathon, this series is built for growth, whether you’re new to trail running or chasing your next big goal. Each race winds through the breathtaking terrain of Babbish Gulch and Sunlight Mountain, offering a mix of beauty, challenge, and pure mountain magic. This is more than a race, it’s a community. name: A Revolutionary Celebration Run
description: Come join us for a FREE 5k on 4th of July at East Jersey Old Town Village. This year we will be having a 5k to kick off our 4th of July celebrations. The run is on paved roads and paths. You will start at the village and run 2 loops of an out and back along Johnson drive which will be closed to traffic. About East Jersey Old Town Village This special historic village has delighted visitors with a glimpse into the past since its opening in 1978. The Village features historic structures from the 1700s and 1800s, reloca­ted to its site within Johnson Pa­rk. They represent different architecture styles found throughout Middlesex County’s Rarita­n Valley. The Village’s founder, Dr. Joseph Kler, and a group of local residents saved most of the buildings from demolition and transported them to the Village where they were reassembled and restored to reflect how they would have looked way back when. name: Iron Horse 4 Miler
description: The Iron Horse 4 miler will raise funds to be donated to the ALS Ride for Life for their patient services at the Stony Brook Neuromuscular Disease and Christopher Pendergast ALS Center of Excellence. A program that provides best-in-class care with a collaborative approach to ensure quality of life for those living with ALS and their families. Currently there is no cure and is always 100% fatal. A note from the race director:My family has had multi-generational familial diagnosis of the fatal disease, Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), commonly known as Lou Gehrig's Disease. ALS is a progressive neurodegenerative disease that affects nerve cells in the brain and spinal cord. Familial ALS accounts for 5 to 10 percent of all ALS cases. This race is honor of my mom, Sally and all those living with ALS and their families.

name: EXTORTION 17 Memorial Run/Ruck - Shadow Events
description: On August 6th 2011, a United States CH-47 Chinook military helicopter operating with the call sign EXTORTION 17 was shot down, marking the most devastating day in Naval Special Warfare history and the single largest loss of life for U.S. forces since the war in Afghanistan began in October 2001. The US military lost 31 warriors that day. Joggin’ for Frogmen was created to honor these heroes and all those who have paid the ultimate sacrifice for our freedom. What began as a single 3.1 mile race in San Diego has expanded to a worldwide event hosting thousands of participants with a mission to to activate communities from around the world to honor the sacrifices of our service members and veterans, and to support the families of our fallen heroes. These races bring communities together to celebrate the lives of America’s fallen and to express our deep gratitude to those still serving. Join us the week of August 6, 2025 and walk, run or ruck to remember.

organizer: Break the Chains: A Walk for Cult Recovery - 2026 International Cult Awareness Month
description: This isn’t just a walk—it’s a movement. Join us for Break the Chains: A Walk for Cult Recovery, a powerful virtual walk/run honoring the courage, resilience, and strength it takes to break free from coercive control and cultic abuse. Whether you’re walking in honor of a survivor, raising awareness in your community, or celebrating your own journey of freedom—every step you take helps shed light on the realities of cultic abuse and the healing that follows. The Glaze Craze 4 Miler isn’t just about speed—it’s about strategy, stomach strength, and a questionable number of life choices. This one-of-a-kind event challenges you to conquer 4 miles of running while taking down 6 donuts along the way. Here's how it goes: Run 1 mile → crush 2 donutsRun 1 mile → crush 2 donutsRun 1 mile → crush 2 donutsFinal mile → sprint (or survive) to the finish Simple on paper. Brutal in reality. This race is a test of pacing, discipline, and your ability to keep it all together—literally. Because here’s the catch: if you throw up at any point… you’re out. DNF. No exceptions. Whether you're chasing a podium spot or just trying to keep your donuts down, the Glaze Craze is equal parts competition and chaos. Expect big energy, loud crowds, and a whole lot of glazzzzzeeee. #RunForIt

name: Extraterrestrial Full Moon
description: Running along the fringe of the mysterious Area 51, this stretch of highway (375) has an overwhelming number of reported UFO sightings. So much so, that in 1996 the federal government officially named highway 375 the "Extraterrestrial Highway". The ET Highway has become a gathering place for UFO enthusiasts and nature lovers alike. With elevations ranging from roughly 4000-5600 feet, the high desert will enchant you with gorgeous vegetation, surrounding mountains, and stunning vistas. An additional treat is the cooler temperatures. Rachel, NV is generally 15 degrees cooler than the Las Vegas Valley; coupled with a night time run, temperatures should be perfect for running in August! * The Extraterrestrial Full Moon Marathon, 1/2, 10K, 5K & 51K are run on the weekend closest to the full moon. Runners will witness as the day falls into night, gorgeous twilight desert glow, a glorious moon rise, shooting stars, and the calm of the vast desert darkness.

description: Summer Biathlon was invented by a group of traditional winter biathletes (cross country skiing and rifle shooting) as a way to continue their training during the summer months. This type of Summer Biathlon consists of three running stages separated by two shooting bouts. Runners are sent off in pairs at one minute intervals. The order of start seeding is determined by an individuals' 5k running time with similar paced runners starting in pairs to minimize congestion in the shooting area. Once a runner starts, he or she will cover a distance of 1500 meters. Upon completion of this first leg, a runner walks to the shooting range and fires 5 shots in the prone position (lying down) with a .22 rifle at 5 knock down targets (a scorer will keep track of hits for each person). Runners then exit the range and run a 2000 meter leg. They then reenter the shooting range and fire 5 shots at the same targets, this time from the standing position. Runners then exit the range and run a final 1500 meter leg to the finish…

name: EXTORTION 17 Memorial Run/Ruck
description: On August 6th 2011, a United States CH-47 Chinook military helicopter operating with the call sign EXTORTION 17 was shot down, marking the most devastating day in Naval Special Warfare history and the single largest loss of life for U.S. forces since the war in Afghanistan began in October 2001. The US military lost 31 warriors that day. Joggin’ for Frogmen was created to honor these heroes and all those who have paid the ultimate sacrifice for our freedom. What began as a single 3.1 mile race in San Diego has expanded to a worldwide event hosting thousands of participants with a mission to to activate communities from around the world to honor the sacrifices of our service members and veterans, and to support the families of our fallen heroes. These races bring communities together to celebrate the lives of America’s fallen and to express our deep gratitude to those still serving. Join us the week of August 6 and walk, run or ruck to remember.

name: Marsh Madness
description: Marsh Madness is a 32-hour ultramarathon on August 7th, 2026. Free fat ass race run on the dikes at Point Mouillee State Game Area, where the Huron River, Detroit River, and Lake Erie converge. Views of Ontario and Ohio across the water await. On the western shores of Lake Erie, Pointe Mouillee State Game Area is one of the most respected waterfowl locations in Michigan. Consisting of 4,040 acres, it is one of the largest freshwater marsh restoration projects in the world. You may see an eagle or a random guy posing with a fish for his Tinder photo. 50 runners max. You supply all of your own aid and nutrition. Crew, pacers, and poles welcome. Elevation gain is 69 feet per loop, 80% gravel, 20% asphalt. Zero water crossings. Temps should be in the 80s. Access to your vehicle every 8 miles. Alternating loops of an 8-mile loop and a 4.6-mile out-and-back during the day. 4-mile loop between the hours of 11 pm and 4 am. 32 hours to complete, with the caveat that we can not run the dike between 11 pm and 6 am. …

Location: Dorchester IA, starting in front of Knotty Marie's on Waterloo Creek Dr. The fun run will head west on Waterloo Creek Drive approximately 1.5 miles and loop back to the starting spot. Purpose: This is a memorial run for Grady Lundgren-Hammel. Grady was an ambitious, loving, energetic boy. He loved agriculture, he loved Dorchester. With approximately 15 miles of diverse, well-maintained trails—including fast open stretches, tight twisty singletrack, fun gravity dips, ravines, meandering paths through prairie and woods, and a perfect mix of technical challenges and flow—this spot is built for adventure and has tested countless runners over the years. Choose from four race distances: The Creeks ~8 Mile, Forest Track Heavy Half and Mountain Lap 5K. Start the weekend off with a test in the Hill Climb-Descent on Friday Night. name: Hoodoo 500
description: The Hoodoo 500 is the most scenic, most challenging, and most rewarding ultra-cycling race on the Planet (in spite of claims by others). The route passes through or around three National Parks, three National Monuments and several Utah State Parks. The scenery varies from majestic cliffs and striking red rock hoodoos to aspen and pine forests and high mountain meadows. You’ll race up mountains over 10,000′ high. You might get hot, you’ll likely get cold. Odds are the wind will at one time be in your face, and another time at your back. You’ll experience many highs and maybe some lows on this amazing journey. And you’ll love every minute! (At least after the fact.) Come join us!

description: Set in beautiful Northeast Michigan, the Aliferis Memorial Race is open to runners, walkers and bikers of all ages and ability levels. description: How long can you go? Join us at Combustion Brewery & Taproom for the Zero Hour Endurance Run, a unique challenge where you’re in control of your distance. name: FXBG Trail 10 Miler
description: The Quarry 10.2 miler is the fifth race in the FXBG Trail series. This race begins with a peaceful stretch along the Rappahannock River, where the Beach Trail hugs the water and the sound of the river sets the rhythm for your stride. The opening miles are smooth and scenic — a calm, steady start that invites you to settle in and enjoy the view before the course begins to build.As you move away from the river, the middle miles introduce a series of rolling hills that keep things lively. These ups and downs are playful but purposeful, testing your pacing and leg turnover while offering just enough recovery on the descents to stay strong. Then comes the finale — one big climb that stands between you and the finish. It’s the defining challenge of the day, steady and demanding, asking for your last reserves of grit. Crest the top, and you’ll carry that hard-earned momentum toward the finish line, knowing you conquered the course from riverbank to summit.

name: 9/11 24 Hour Ruck
description: Join us as we honor and remember the lives lost, the heroes who emerged, and the resilience of our nation on the 25th anniversary of September 11th, 2001. Participants will ruck the 2.2 mile out-and-back boardwalk along the Sakonnet River, starting at Battleship Cove for a full day, carrying both the physical weight of their packs and the symbolic weight of that day. This is not a race, it's a tribute. Participants are encouraged to come and go as they are able, rucking any distance that feels meaningful to them. Whether you join for a single mile or commit to multiple laps throughout the day and night, every step taken is a step in honor of those who served, sacrificed, and stood in the face of tragedy. Together, we will move with purpose, reflect with gratitude, and stand united in remembrance. All are welcome - veterans, active duty, first responders, families, supporters, and friends. Lace up, shoulder your pack, and be part of something that matters.

BRR consists of maximum 12 person (4 person minimum) teams that rotate through 36 transition areas as they cover the approximate 208 mile distance of the race. The Start! BRR starts in Grayson Highlands State Park, VA at an elevation of 4920′, near the base of Mount Rogers (5729′), the highest peak in Virginia. The Highlands’ defining feature are the high elevation balds that are spotted with stands of native Fraser Fir, boulder fields and a herd of wild ponies. name: Top Gun Night Run 6k
description: The Capt. Jeff Kuss USMC Memorial hosts the annual Top Gun Night Run 6k on Friday, September 11 at 7:30 p.m. in Lee Victory Recreation Park in Smyrna. On June 2, 2016, our nation was deeply impacted by the plane crash of USMC Captain Jeff Kuss during the US Navy Blue Angels performance at the Great Tennessee Air Show, in Smyrna. Following this tragedy, the Smyrna community and Blue Angels fans around the country mourned and showed an outpouring of support for the Kuss Family. Town of Smyrna officials called upon the community to help establish a living memorial in tribute to the life, honorable service, and high ideals exhibited by Captain Kuss. name: MAMELE MOUNTAINS
description: Mamele Mountains is a women’s only 8 mile trail run through some of the most beautiful terrain in the country. This race is for YOU. Whether you’re a seasoned racer or someone ready to tackle their first trail run, you belong here. Women from all walks of life, backgrounds, and fitness levels come together every year to face this mountain...and they leave stronger, braver, and more connected than ever. Get ready to be challenged by rugged terrain and climbs that test you both physically and mentally. Our promise: you’ll leave the mountain better, stronger, and inspired--surrounded by women who lift each other higher. Let’s climb together.

description: If you've ever experienced fall in the Rocky Mountains you know what a magical time it is. With cool temperatures, sunny days, and stunning scenery, many people believe autumn is the best time to get out and enjoy the high country. And while a drive up through the mountains in the fall can be a nice way to spend a day, we think you should take it one step further. We think you should get out and experience it on foot! The Flaming Foliage Relay takes the best parts of the old Outward Bound Relay route and throws in some new and scenic challenges. This relay begins in the quaint town of Idaho Springs and traverses 165 miles and three rugged mountain passes before finishing in charming Buena Vista on the banks of the Arkansas River. Along the way you'll run on roads and trails through some of the most amazing scenery Colorado has to offer. description: Get out of the city and join us for another race with Soil Mates Trail Races. Run on beautiful private trails with fresh air, fun running mates, and no pavement over rich Georgia soil. We honor all of those who lost their lives on September 11, 2001 and support our first responders and military who make extraordinary sacrifices in the line of duty! description: The 2nd Annual Cane Creek Mountain Trail Run features 10K or Half Marathon of seriously stellar single-track, and at the tail end of the race, an optional stair climb to the top of the 80′ observation tower, offering spectacular views from the highest peak in NC east of Greensboro. Cane Creek Mountain Natural Area is a new 1000 acre park located in Snow Camp, NC (Alamance County) and is an easy drive from Chapel Hill, Durham, Raleigh, Burlington, Greensboro, and Winston-Salem. name: duckDNA Application Portal
description: Welcome to the duckDNA application portal, your first step to becoming a hunter-scientist through duckDNA. This portal streamlines the application process for all of our projects. Whether you are interested in our standard sampling program, in which participants harvest and contribute samples from three Mallard-like ducks (Mallard, American Black Duck, Mexican Duck, or Mottled Duck), or the hybrid sampling program, which focuses on hybrids or other visually distinctive ducks already in hand, our secure and user-friendly tools make it easy to get involved. By applying, you become a vital part of a ground-breaking research project. Through this project, we are revealing the prevalence of game-farm Mallard genes in wild populations, exploring Mallard population structure, discovering new hybrids, and laying the foundation for a deeper understanding of how genetics controls waterfowl behavior and ecology. name: Coop's Loop Endurance Run
description: Coop's Loop Endurance Run is a 6-hour timed event on a 2.1 mile looped course. The goal is to run, walk, or hike as many loops as possible within the 6-hour event! Awards will be given to the top 3 males, females, and relay teams. The fastest loop by an open male and female will also be awarded. Coop’s Loop is a 2.1-mile trail loop with 400 feet of gain and descent, designed to test your legs, reward your focus, and keep you coming back for more. description: The goal of A Pace for Petey is to bring about awareness to overdose/drug addiction and recovery. It will begin in the south parking lot of Tuscola High school, close to his final resting place, and end with a lap on the track around the TCHS football field, where he played many, many football games and ran on the track team. New this year is a kids fun run, called Jake's Jog! It is in honor of Jacob (Petey's brother), who also lost his battle to substance use, on May 29, 2019, at the age of 29. His resting place is right next to his brother. Jacob always drove the golf cart sag wagon at A Pace for Petey, prior to losing his battle. Jake's jog is for kids 10 and under. name: The AlKEMist Gravel Fest
description: The AlKemist Gravel Fest — October 4, 2025 | Mandan, North Dakota Brewed for the Bold. Born on Gravel. The AlKemist Gravel Fest was first brewed up in 2018 after exploring some of the most rugged and rewarding gravel roads in Morton County, North Dakota. Now it’s one of the region’s most anticipated fall gravel races — bringing together cyclists who crave challenge, community, and an unbeatable view. Start your adventure at Graner Park / Sugarloaf Bottoms, just south of Mandan, ND, where you’ll climb out of the Missouri River Valley and onto the bluffs of Morton County. Every mile serves up fast descents, minimum-maintenance roads, and some of the longest climbs in the region — all balanced by wide-open prairie skies and unforgettable scenery. When the dust settles, join us for post-race awards, hot food fresh off the grill, and a celebration worthy of the miles you’ve conquered.

name: Capalbo Strong Walk
description: The Capalbo Strong Walk is a community event held to honor Charlie Capalbo, a beloved son, brother, teammate, and friend whose strength, humor, and resilience inspired everyone around him. Founded in 2017 by a group of Fairfield Prep hockey moms during Charlie’s first battle with cancer, Capalbo Strong began as a way to rally support for him and his family. Over the next five years, Charlie courageously fought and beat cancer three times, facing both Non-Hodgkin’s Lymphoma and Leukemia with remarkable grit and an unwavering positive spirit. Tragically, he passed away in April 2022, just one month shy of his 24th birthday. Walk participants are asked to pay the registration fee and raise a minimum of $300 to help make a meaningful impact. Virtual participants are asked to pay the registration fee and raise a minimum of $100. (Fundraising is waived for Kids under 12!) New this year, the 24K starts and finishes at Jennings Beach, keeping the entire experience close to home! Don’t let the full 15 miles intimidate…

description: Ashure Ministry, Hickory Soup Kitchen, and The Corner Table are proud to come together to host the 2026 Catawba County Hunger Walk! We invite you to join us for this meaningful community event dedicated to fighting hunger right here in Catawba County. Proceeds from this year’s walk will support all three organizations as we work together to provide food, hope, and dignity to our neighbors facing food insecurity. The Hunger Walk is more than just a fundraiser—it’s a powerful way to bring our community together while raising awareness about the ongoing challenge of hunger in our area. We humbly ask for your support. Every dollar raised will be divided equally among Ashure Ministry, Hickory Soup Kitchen, and The Corner Table, and every dollar goes directly toward helping feed those who need it most. name: MightyMan Montauk
description: Athletes enjoy this course for its beauty and small-town atmosphere. Montauk is a quaint fishing and surfing town on the easternmost tip of Long Island. The town is known for its natural beauty and sports enthusiastic visitors. Montauk is one of the birthplaces of triathlon. The sport is growing and athletes want to challenge themselves with longer events. There are few metro area triathlons of this distance. In addition to providing a venue for the athletes, this event will showcase Montauk at a time when the weather is still nice but the summer crowds are not as heavy. This is a great family weekend to spend on the east end with the Olympic and Sprint triathlons both taking place on Sunday.

name: Kettle Cooker Trail Race
description: Explore the scenic Glenroy Preserve trails at the fourth annual Kettle Cooker Five & Dime on October 4th, 2026 presented by Herr's Snacks and Altra Running, along with many local sponsors! It takes a village! Glenroy Preserve is a beautiful outdoor playground that also happens to be rich in history. Some of the trails will take you through parts of the Underground Railroad, while even running past a tavern that was said to have served patrons during the Civil War. Each distance is a loop. All distances will follow the same course, however the 5 mile runners will split around mile 4 to the finish. ALL distances offer plenty of hills, creek crossings, mixed terrain, and plenty of on-course support. The 50K is two loops of the 25K. You should wear trail shoes for this race, as there are numerous creek crossings and mixed terrain to traverse. Your feet WILL get wet and trail shoes offer the best drainage and traction. We will have a 1K Fun Run that starts at 8:00am. The 5K begins at 8:30am. Both races start on Broad St and finish in front of the Statham Elementary School Gym. The running club at SES is for 4th and 5th graders and the earnings will go to much needed running clothes and apparel for the students. The running club at BCMS includes 6th, 7th and 8th graders. The rolling hills are not extreme, though the final stretch can be a nice uphill challenge. At the finish line are healthy eats and drinks for each participant designed to speed your recovery. name: Camino De Los Muertos
description: Saturday, October 31st , 2026. This incredible natural area (now known as LLELA) was originally wild and beautiful, full of an endless number of native species. But the area around it became urbanized and the city moved in on it. LLELA was tamed, eventually being surrounded by suburbia (the city, and thousands of people and noise). Now, LLELA, University of North Texas, and the City of Lewisville are working to bring back the wild. Reclaiming it, protecting it, and making beautiful experiences possible for generations to come. As they work daily to restore and replenish the native plant, tree, and animal life, they are bringing the natural environment back full circle. We invite you to come take part in that process, and enjoy these special trails and eco-systems, while showing your support for LLELA’s great work! name: Whitney's Race 2026
description: Whitney's Race is not just Whitney's race. It is a race against time for those yet to be afflicted with pancreatic cancer, the most deadly cancer. It is Time To Cure® pancreatic cancer. Whitney's Time To Cure® has passed. Whitney Marsh perished at age 41, November 1, 2018, ten months after diagnosis with pancreatic cancer. Five-year survival from pancreatic cancer stands at 6-9% showing little to no improvement in survival in the past 50 years despite vast medical advances across almost all other cancers. Pancreatic cancer is currently the number two cancer killer in 2020 and researchers estimate pancreatic cancer will be the number one by 2030. Diagnosis is often late begetting the need for local medical practitioner education as well as research for improved diagnostic testing and imaging. Once a diagnosis of pancreatic cancer has been made treatment usually involves chemotherapy with or without radiation therapy followed by curative intent surgery followed by more chemotherapy. This isn't just any race—it's a race with your dog! Bring your four-legged pal and dress them up in their best Halloween costume for a chance to win our doggy costume contest. Whether you're walking, jogging, or running, you'll be doing it alongside fellow dog lovers in a festive, Halloween-themed atmosphere. After the race, stick around for a variety of fun activities, including a bob for apples contest, a basket raffle with exciting prizes, and more! It's the perfect way to spend a fall day while supporting The American Service Dog Foundation. Every dollar raised goes toward training and donating service dogs to individuals with disabilities, making a real difference in their lives. Don't miss out on this howling good time! Run it solo. Run it as a team.Either way, the challenge is the same. The course is a .84-mile paved loop inside Riverside Park. You’ll start and finish in the same place every lap—near the gazebo and caboose. No guesswork. No point-to-point logistics. Just rhythm. This race is for anyone willing to stay in it a little longer than they’re used to.

name: Old Florida Gravel
description: "Old Florida" describes a bygone era long before theme parks, mega-resorts, HOAs, and pickleball.Google it...it's actually a thing. These dirt roads will take you back in time. Live oak trees with Spanish moss hanging off their branches have been there for 100yrs. Cool crystal clear springs becon just minutes from the venue. More cows than people along the route will surprise you. Roadside fruit stands selling oranges and watermelon await. Front porches and sipping sweet tea are local past times. Old Florida Gravel will challenge you physically and reward you mentally. The miles pedaled will transport you to a forgotten era that you are certain to never forget!

Each run is dedicated to raising awareness about parental alienation, family court practices that separate children from a loving parent, and the urgent need for children to have reasonable access to both parents. Parental alienation and unnecessary parent-child separation cause long-term emotional, psychological, and developmental harm. This run exists to bring visibility to that harm and to advocate for fair, child-focused family court outcomes. This event is Run 11 of 50. description: The Iceman Cometh Challenge, presented by Trek, takes place on Saturday, November 7, 2026. The Ice Cycle Expo and packet pickup, presented by Michigan Bicycle Law, will be held Friday, November 6 at the Grand Traverse Resort in Acme, MI. More than 5,400 men and women, along with 600 children across 77 age divisions, participate in Iceman weekend each year. The signature event is a roughly 30-mile point-to-point cross-country mountain bike race from Kalkaska to Traverse City, Michigan. Additional events include the Meijer Slush Cup, Sno-Cone, and Pop-Cycle races, featuring a 9-mile beginner-friendly course and youth races for children 10 and under. Nearly 12,000 spectators line the course annually to experience the excitement of Iceman weekend.

description: This memorial race is held in memory of Joe Mike Baker. Joe Mike lived and worked in the Sandy Bottom Community. At the time of his accidental death in September 2014, he was training for his first half marathon. As a tribute and to honor his memory, family and friends organized the JMB Memorial 5K and Fun Run to raise money for scholarships for high school seniors who plan to use their education to give back to their community just as Joe Mike did. Through the generous donations of the sponsors and commitment of the runners and volunteers, since 2016, the JMB Memorial 5K and Fun Run has awarded more than $34,000.00 in scholarships to 37 South Lenoir High School students. name: Pocantico Hills Races
description: Take on a breathtaking course through the Rockefeller State Preserve, where trails built over a century ago wind past stunning scenery at every turn! Start and finish at Rockwood Hall, with sweeping views of the Hudson River and the Palisades, just off Route 9 in Sleepy Hollow, next to Phelps Hospital. Both the half-marathon and marathon are single-loop adventures on wide, groomed carriage roads, with the marathon showcasing nearly all of the park’s signature sights. Climb and roll past fields, historic stone walls, charming bridges, grazing livestock, sparkling rivers, lush forests, and peaceful lakes; no pavement, no cars, just pure trail bliss. These races are walk-friendly and offer generous cutoff times, so runners of every pace can join in the fun. Whether you’re chasing a personal best or simply exploring one of the Hudson Valley’s most scenic and historic preserves, the Pocantico Hills Races promise an unforgettable experience!

name: Bobcat
description: Prepare to immerse yourself in the rugged beauty of Burr Oak State Park at Bobcat. This trail marathon and half marathon offers a unique opportunity for trail running enthusiasts and hikers to experience the wild and challenging terrain of Ohio wilderness. The marathon's single-loop course provides a diverse and scenic adventure, featuring rolling hills, several creek crossings, and portions of the Buckeye Trail. The half marathon offers an equally thrilling point-to-point experience on the same trails as the marathon. This race is all about embracing the untamed beauty of Burr Oak – 90% of the course is pure trail! Whether you're a seasoned trail runner, a hiker, or new to the trails, all are welcome and encouraged to come and experience the Bobcat adventure at your own pace. Bobcat is your chance to get wild, be challenged, and reconnect with nature on an extraordinary course in one of Ohio's most pristine state parks.

description: Marmon Valley Farm is hosting the Horseshoe Hill Climb 5K, 10K and 20K trail run on Saturday, November 7, 2026 at 9am to raise money that will help kids come to summer horse camp. These funds make it possible for children from economically challenged families to attend camp and helps in sustaining other areas necessary for the ministry. Many of the trails throughout Marmon Valley's 500 acres are bridle trails, farm lanes, and open meadows providing a fantastic trail running experience! The trails and terrain at Marmon Valley are ideal for trail racers who are looking for a challenging run. Whatever distance chosen, you will traverse through hardwood forest, up and down ravine trails, around fields, across creeks, and along scenic overlooks. name: KF5K
description: Join us for the KF5K! One hundred percent of the proceeds from this community event will benefit The Scholarship Fund in Memory of Kevin Flach. Kevin was a fun-loving, energetic, 6 year-old boy who loved the Phillies and playing with his siblings and friends at St. Luke School. It is the hope of all of Kevin’s loved ones to keep his name and spirit alive through the Kevin Flach Scholarship Fund. The intent of the scholarship fund is to not only keep Kevin’s spirit alive, but to continue to provide someone less fortunate a scholarship to St. Luke School. Both of Kevin’s parents insisted on such a fund. They have six other children who all graduated from St. Luke School, and they believe it is a great way to honor his extraordinary life.

name: Scott Sterrett Memorial Races
description: The Scott Sterrett Memorial Race Weekend returns on Saturday, November 7th, 2026. We are continuing the traditions you love: 5K, 10K, scenic Half Marathon, Hero Bibs, and incredible race swag! Scott Sterrett was a reserve officer for the City of Cedar Falls beginning in May of 2005. Scott was a member of Nazareth Lutheran Church. He was an avid runner participating in 23 marathons total, the Boston Marathon twice, and the Chicago and Dallas Marathons multiple times. In addition to his passion for running, Scott had a passion for being a reserve officer with the Cedar Falls Police Department and serving his community. In 2018, Scott passed away after a fight with pancreatic cancer. This event is dedicated to Scott. A portion of the proceeds from the event will be put into a scholarship for local seniors who plan to pursue a career as a first responder. Our goal for this event is to continue to build a strong relationship between the community and those that serve us every day.

name: The Redder for Edder Run
description: Please join us and wear red as we come together to remember Edder and support his family. At 1:50AM on Sunday November 2nd, the Normal Fire Department bravely responded to a house fire. On Saturday November 22nd we invite the Community to gather at Maxwell Park for this 3 Mile Run/Walk to benefit and remember Edder and honor his family. All proceeds will go to Edder's Family as they work through this unimaginable tragedy. The 3 Mile Run/Walk kicks off at 9AM. The entry fee has been kept low to encourage the community to attend and show support. Donations are encouraged and accepted. An apparel store is open for a limited time: https://orders.minervapromotions.com/redder_for_edder/shop/home

name: Hillacious Half Marathon
description: Why We Run The Hillacious Half was created to honor our military — to thank them and ensure their sacrifices are never taken for granted. The course is intentionally tough, representing the effort and endurance our service members face every day, often far from their families. This is a bare bones race with no prize money and no frills — just grit, sweat, and the satisfaction of finishing one of the toughest courses around. All proceeds after race expenses go into a fund to support local military personnel and families who need a helping hand. Funds are distributed directly through the Hillacious Half, never to large agencies. Both the first-place male and female finishers have their names engraved on perpetual trophies housed at the Morgan-Weir American Legion Post 27 in Litchfield. We run this race in honor of those who serve and have served — carrying their strength with us up every hill. description: Outrun Krampus: The Sunset 5K Challenge Brace yourself for a unique, twilight 5K cross country race. We're setting the course on the beautiful Pike Red Devil XC Course, a hidden slice of nature tucked behind Eastbrook Elementary in the heart of Indianapolis. The challenge? name: Shakori 40 Running Festival
description: The Shakori 40 brings the running community together for a celebration of nature, team camaraderie, and live music. We offer a 40-mile ultramarathon, a 40K open race for men and women, and a 40-mile age-graded team relay for up to 10 members—factoring in age and gender to determine the overall winning team. There’s also a 4-mile open race. Our cross-country style course winds through the Shakori Hills Community Art Center in Pittsboro, NC. Shakori Hills, located just outside Chapel Hill, NC, is renowned for the Shakori Hills Music Festival. The Community Art Center is a place where everyone can enjoy nature, walk scenic trails, spend sunny afternoons with family, and immerse themselves in art, music, and life’s simple pleasures. By embracing these abundant resources, our local culture continues to thrive. You’ll have a blast at the Shakori 40, thanks to great camaraderie, live music, delicious food, camping, bonfires, craft beer, and so much more. Join us each December for a weekend you’ll never forget!…

description: Welcome to the Crooked Creek Ultra, an exhilarating trail race set in the heart of Bourbon Country at the picturesque Camp Crooked Creek inside the Harry S. Frazier Scout Reservation. description: December 5th, 2026 Sponsored by Altra Running and NeverSecond Western States 100 Lottery Qualifier (sub 32-hour 100-mile) with 119 qualifiers in 2024 and 133 qualifier in 2025! This is the December edition of our popular Brazos Bend races, with the marquee event being the 100-mile. The Brazos Bend 100 is the largest trail race in Texas and one of the fastest trail races in the world on flat and smooth trails with incredible support from aid stations on a multi-loop course. The top 3 runners were under 16 hours in 2024. The course is 99.9% flat, and the only "hill" is a 10-foot rise over 0.1 of a mile. The rest of the ~16.7mi loop is flat surfaces that move from hard crushed rock, soft hiking trails under tree canopy, and smooth horse trails. Most runners will use a road shoe like the Altra Vanish Carbon 2, Torin 8, or Flow 2 but under wetter conditons a trail shoe may be a better choice. In 2021, this event was moved to its new home at Staunton State Park in Pine, CO featuring 50k, 16-Mile, and 8-Mile distance options. Staunton State Park is a gem within Colorado’s State Park system. From high grassy meadows at 8,100 feet to soaring granite cliffs over 10,000 feet, Staunton State Park’s varied geology, soils, water features, and climate support rare and unexpected plant communities and a rich diversity of wildlife and provide a myriad of outdoor recreation opportunities. The park is located approximately 40 miles southwest of downtown Denver, north of US Highway 285 and about six miles west of Conifer in Pine, CO. name: Emerald Coast Ultra
description: From the white-sand shores of Big Lagoon State Park to the storied walls of Fort Morgan Historic Site, this 50 Mile and 50K journey is more than a race — it’s a coastal odyssey. Runners begin at sunrise beneath whispering pines and the salty breeze of the Gulf Coast. The air hangs thick with anticipation as feet press into soft sand and smooth coastal pavement, tracing the edge of emerald waters. Pelicans glide overhead. The rhythm of the tide sets the tempo. The sun climbs higher, casting a golden shimmer across the water — beautiful, relentless, unforgettable. name: OUTLAST SAN ANTONIO
description: What Is OUTLAST? OUTLAST is a 6-hour trail endurance challenge where runners complete a 5K every hour, on the hour. Each lap must be finished within the hour to stay in the event. If you finish early, you rest until the next round. Miss a lap, and you’re out. Complete all six rounds, and you OUTLAST. This isn't just about speed — it's about pacing, discipline, and mental grit. Whether you're trying to survive all six or win your division, the challenge is the same: show up each hour, push your limits, and stay in it. Each course is trail-based, with natural terrain, elevation, and unpredictable conditions. You’ll have time between rounds to recover, refuel, and refocus — but not much. What You Earn: ​4 laps = “Grit Earned” patch5 laps = “Survivor” patch6 laps = Premium “OUTLAST” medal​​All participants receive an OUTLAST Tee.
